answer: Neighborhood Convergence Scoring. Each agent's score is the overlap between its transaction partners and those partners' partners; a new agent inherits a map slot in the shared atlas only when its neighborhood folds back on itself. Isolated clusters diverge, so a fresh identity produces a plume of one-off links that decays without recursive reinforcement. Duplicates therefore cannot borrow trust: each must independently sustain a ripple of returning counterparties. Enforcement: agents below the fold-back threshold lose routing priority.
